## Claims
- [source-backed] For \(m\ge1\), source-30 takes \(n=4m\), \(r=s=2m\), \(i=j=m\), hence \(a=b=m\), but states \(\binom{2m}{m}\) only “according to Conjecture 4.10.” [doi:10.1090/s0002-9947-2010-05163-3, lines 938-955]
- [proved] Let \(A_m=H^\star(GL_{4m}/B,\mathbb Z)\), \(v_m=v_{2m,2m,m+1,4m}\), and let \(w_m=w_{2m,2m,m+1,4m}\). Then
  \[
  J_{v_m}^{A_m}=I_{w_m}^{A_m},\qquad
  \mu_{A_m}(J_{v_m}^{A_m})=\mu_{A_m}(I_{w_m}^{A_m}).
  \]
  Indeed \(m+1\le2m\) and \(m+1>0=2m+2m-4m\), so \(v_m\) is an admissible bigrassmannian. The dissector property gives
  \[
  S_{4m}=\{u:u\ge v_m\}\sqcup\{u:u\le w_m\},
  \]
  hence \(u\ge v_m\iff u\not\le w_m\). Since integral Schubert classes are a homogeneous \(\mathbb Z\)-basis of \(A_m\), the defining spans of \(J_{v_m}^{A_m}\) and \(I_{w_m}^{A_m}\) are literally equal. Thus their homogeneous generating sets, and therefore their minimum cardinalities \(\mu_{A_m}\), coincide. [doi:10.1090/s0002-9947-2010-05163-3, lines 61-66, 603-620, 664-683]
- [unsupported] No supplied internal theorem with a durable locator asserts
  \[
  \mu_{A_m}(J_{v_m}^{A_m})=\binom{2m}{m}\quad(m\ge1).
  \]
  The available source instead makes that equality conditional on Conjecture 4.10. [artifact 195d651f74f369c392a9d9789becba3f3b5fd7ec8f2a6876a4cbf230fd4ead91, lines 1-65]

## Strategy
The reduction preserves generator number because it identifies the two ideals inside the same integral graded ring \(A_m\), not merely via a Grassmannian-subring generating family.

## Gaps
The required numerical theorem in \(A_m\) is absent. Consequently, the numerical certificate is not established; only the reduction’s preservation of \(\mu\) is proved.

## Next
A durably located theorem or independent proof of \(\mu_{A_m}(J_{v_m}^{A_m})=\binom{2m}{m}\) is required.
